title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1RC0LD_1LA0RB_1LB1LE_1RF0LA_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1RC0LD_1LA0RB_1LB1LE_1RF0LA_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, but it is now a question about numbers. Lean proves (kernel only) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of 22 under an explicit map reaches a halt: halts_iff in lean/Orbit.lean. The map is N → 3N + 24 + 6j − 20·2j, and it halts exactly when the remainder mj = N + 10 − 10·2j + 2j is 0. 106 rounds of the map do not halt; no residue class rules a halt out, and the chance of a halt later is heuristically below 10−200000.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,905 cells have been visited and 24,859 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.538). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.084).

claims.title: One-pass rules
claims.text: Nine rules, each for all values of its counts: the first pass and the zigzag of a doubling, its last pass, the three ways a doubling phase can run out of 1s, the transfer of two 1s into a pair 10, the end of a round and the halting case.

claims.title: A doubling, for every size
claims.text: From state D at the left end of (10)^(K+1) 1^(c+2K+8) the machine reaches state D at the left end of (10)^(2K+6) 1^c (the zigzag chained by induction).

claims.title: The end of a round
claims.text: From (10)^K 1^m with m even and 2 ≤ m < 2K+6 the machine reaches 10 1^(2K+3m+2); from (10)^K with no 1s (K ≥ 1) it halts.

claims.title: Halts if and only if the orbit of 22 hits a halt
claims.text: From blank tape the machine reaches D> 10 1^22 after 208 steps, and it halts from blank tape if and only if some orbit i = none, where orbit iterates next N = phase 1 N from 22.

claims.title: The closed form of the map, checked against the machine
claims.text: With j the number of doublings (the least j ≥ 1 with 20·2<sup>j</sup> > N + 12 + 2j), the remainder is m = N + 10 − 10·2<sup>j</sup> + 2j and N' = 3N + 24 + 6j − 20·2<sup>j</sup>. The C program runs the machine from every even N from 8 to 3000 and agrees with this formula every time, including the halts at N = 8, 26, 64, 142, 300, 618, 1256, 2534 (the values N = 10·2<sup>j</sup> − 2j − 10).

claims.title: 10<sup>6</sup> rounds without a halt
claims.text: Iterating the map from 22 with exact integers: no halt in the first 10<sup>6</sup> rounds; N then has 666,845 bits. The closest approach of m to 0, relative to its range 10·2<sup>j</sup>, is 3.8·10<sup>−6</sup> (round 736,098), about what uniform sampling predicts for a million rounds.

claims.title: Probviously nonhalting
claims.text: m is spread over a range of about 10·2<sup>j</sup> values (even ones only), and its residues mod small numbers look uniform along the orbit, so round i halts with chance about 1/(5·2<sup>j</sup>); j grows by about 0.67 per round. After the rounds already checked (j is then about 667,000), the total chance of a halt is below 10<sup>−200000</sup>.

claims.title: Does the orbit of 22 ever reach m = 0?
claims.text: Not known: a Collatz-like question about the map above (a cryptid in the bbchallenge sense).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the question is now about numbers. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs in rounds; each round reads a number N off the tape and writes a bigger one, and Lean proves that the machine halts exactly when one round finds a remainder of 0. This page shows how a round works, the map it computes, and why a halt looks hopeless.

facts.text: The machine halts iff the orbit of 22 under the round map ever has remainder 0 (Lean, kernel).
The map iterated a million rounds from 22 without a halt.
Rough chance of a halt in all later rounds.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Pairs and ones
html: Write a for the pair 10. At the start of every round the whole tape is a 1^N (one pair, then N ones, blank on both sides) and the head is in state D on the left end. The first round starts at N = 22, after 208 steps.

A round has two parts. First come doublings: the machine zigzags between the pairs on the left and the ones on the right, moving one pair at a time across and turning two 1s into a new pair each time; one doubling turns a^K 1^m into a^(2K+4) 1^(m-2K-6). So the block of pairs grows 1, 6, 16, 36, 76, … = 5·2j − 4 while the ones are eaten. Then, when fewer than 2K+6 ones are left, the remainder m is folded back: every pair turns back into ones, and the next round starts at N' = 2K + 3m + 2.

The left side of the tape barely moves (that is the slow, logarithmic side); the ones grow by a factor between 1 and 2 per round, and each round costs about N2 steps, so the tape grows like the square root of the time.

sections.heading: The round map
html:
After j doublings the pairs number K = 5·2j − 4 and the ones mj = N + 10 − 10·2j + 2j. The doublings stop at the first j with mj < 10·2j − 2. Then

N' = 3N + 24 + 6j − 20·2j   (if mj > 0),   halt   (if mj = 0).

N stays even, so m does too. Since 20·2j lies between N and 2N, N' lies between N and 2N.
The column "step reached" is the step at which the machine is in state D at the left end of a 1^N, read off a direct simulation; the other columns are the map.

sections.heading: A halt needs a remainder of exactly zero
html: If a doubling phase ever starts with no 1s at all (m = 0), the head runs off the right end of a^K in state F onto a blank cell, and F0 is the halting transition. That happens exactly when N = 10·2j − 2j − 10: N = 8, 26, 64, 142, 300, … Started there, the machine does halt (checked for N up to 3000). Lean proves the whole equivalence: halts_iff says the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of 22 reaches such a value.

The orbit of 22 misses them for at least a million rounds. Along the orbit the remainder m looks like a random even number below 10·2j, with no bias in any residue class we tried, so each round has a chance of roughly 1/(5·2j) to halt, and j grows by about two thirds per round. That is the shape of a cryptid: the machine almost certainly never halts, but proving it would mean controlling a Collatz-like orbit, which nobody knows how to do.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.538). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.084).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,905 cells (32,802 left of the start, 47 right), with a density of 1s of 0.623.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Collatz-like doubling counter: halts iff the remainder m of a doubling phase is ever exactly 0; the reduction to a map on numbers is proved in Lean.
